top.title: John Collins scores season-high to lead Pistons to victory over Wizards
top.description: DETROIT — Coach J.B. Bickerstaff was speechless when asked about the Detroit Pistons ' slow starts. He offered no response after the Pistons scored just 14 first-quarter points in Sunday night's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers . Twenty-four hours later, Bickerstaff addressed the Pistons' poor start by changing his starting lineup, which included Daniss Jenkins replacing Paul Reed. The decision left the Pistons with a considerable size disadvantage against one of the league's tallest teams. However, this strategy led to one of their most productive first quarters of the season and a 122-111 victory on Monday night, Nov. 9, inside Little Caesars Arena. Bickerstaff's lineup change addressed the Pistons' struggles that led to their recent two-game losing streak; however, it seemed to benefit John Collins the most. Collins came into the game having scored in double figures once over the previous six games and averaging 6.3 points and 4.7 rebounds. The game against the Lakers was arguably Collins' worst performance, and at times he looked visibly upset with his play. Against the Wizards, Collins set an early tone for the Pistons by scoring nine of the team's first 18 points. Each time the Wizards tried to mount a rally, Collins either scored a timely basket or his defense helped stop Washington's run. While starting at center amid Bickerstaff's lineup change, Collins finished with a season-high 24 points on 9-for-13 shooting and 10 rebounds. The highlight of the night that showcased Collins' motivation to bounce back came at 7:19 in the first quarter, when he completed an alley-oop from Ausar Thompson. The basket forced Wizards coach Brian Keefe to call a timeout. As players walked back to their benches, Collins celebrated passionately. Duncan Robinson continued his impressive start to the season, adding 22 points on 4-for-8 shooting from three, while Jenkins followed up his career performance against the Lakers with 20 points on 7-for-16 shooting, plus eight assists and five rebounds. The main criticism of Collins was his inability to defend Anthony Davis, which also highlighted a broader issue for Detroit. Returning from a two-game absence due to a foot injury, Davis showed why the Pistons reportedly pursued him at the trade deadline last year, finishing with a season-high 44 points on 16-for-20 shooting and 13 rebounds. He scored 30 points on 10-for-11 shooting in the first half. Davis scored effortlessly from the inside, taking advantage of the Pistons' lack of size, especially without Jalen Duren, who missed his eighth straight game with a hamstring strain. Trae Young put together an inefficient 20 points on 3-for-10 shooting from beyond the arc, but the Wizards also showcased why they have a bright future: AJ Dybantsa, the reigning No. 1 pick of the 2026 NBA Draft. top.title: Hornets humiliate the Cavs 124-112
top.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 9: James Harden #1 and Evan Mobley #4 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 9, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers, in desperate need of a get-right game, put together one of their worst performances in recent (regular season) memory by getting blown out by the Charlotte Hornets 124-112 on Monday night. The Cavs fall a game under .500 before heading to New York on Wednesday to play the defending champion Knicks on national television. Instead of using tonight’s game as a momentum builder, the Cavs were laughed out of the arena by the woeful Hornets. Cleveland trailed by as many as 33 points against the NBA’s worst offense in Charlotte, a team that was already missing several key players. Grayson Allen (27 points on 8/14 shooting) and Naz Reid (25 points, 13 rebounds) thoroughly outplayed Cleveland’s starters, resulting in a 16-point deficit at the half. That ballooned to 27 points at the end of the third quarter, leading to none of the Cavs’ starters returning to the game after that. Jarrett Allen returned to the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points and seven rebounds in 19 minutes. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden had 11 points each and combined to shoot 7-20 from the floor. Harden in particular was disastrous, and had some of the worst defensive possessions you will ever see from an NBA player. Evan Mobley had an exceptionally ineffective game, too, with nine points and four turnovers. Harden and Mobley had a combined +/- of -46 tonight, which passes the eye test. Not only did Charlotte’s starters outplay the Cavs, but Cleveland’s backups did too. Craig Porter Jr., Thomas Bryant, Thomas, and Norchad Omier brought the Cavs within eight points late in the fourth quarter before running out of steam. But the reserves showed a lot of heart, and considerably more effort and energy than Cleveland’s starters. The Cavs were out rebounded 49-32 overall, but didn’t get their first offensive rebound until the third quarter, losing that battle 17-3. Cleveland actually ended up with fewer turnovers and shot better from the floor than Charlotte, but the final score didn’t reflect that. This is the type of loss that reverberates through an organization, especially one that is expensive and on a fixed timeline like the Cavs. There is a heightened sense of urgency to right the ship, but Cleveland remains exceptionally inconsistent and underwhelming. Despite quality wins against Minnesota and Philadelphia, the Cavs feel like a team teetering on the edge of the abyss. Losses like tonight’s are what push things over.

Russell Wilson shared a touching message in honor of his late father’s birthday. “I miss you Dad. Happy Birthday 🕊️🕊️🕊️,” Wilson wrote on X. Wilson’s father, Harrison Wilson III, died in 2010 at the age of 55 due to complications from diabetes. Today would have been his 71st birthday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In 2015, the Super Bowl champion shared how much his father meant to him in a letter to the Player’s Tribune for Father’s Day and how he supported him in his early days in football before he graced an NFL field. He recalled the time he was the coach for his YMCA basketball team. “We were the Lakers,” Wilson wrote of the youth basketball team. “We ended up winning the championship, and I just remember how he was smiling from ear to ear as all the kids were jumping around like we just won an NBA title.” Wilson also played baseball alongside Pop Warner growing up, and shared that his dad loved to sing while on road trips to his games and practices. Since his father died in 2010, he didn’t get to see him win his Super Bowl championship in 2014 as the Seattle Seahawks quarterback. The retired NFL star looked up to his father and was determined to replicate the kind of dad he was to his own kids in the future. “I know that I will have a big family one day, and if I can be 1/16th of the dad my father was to me, I know I will be an unbelievable dad,” he wrote at the time. “I will try to motivate my kids the way he motivated me and teach them that they can really, truly do anything.” Wilson is now a father of four with one on the way with wife Ciara. top.title: Doc Rivers Apologized To Giannis Antetokounmpo After Criticizing His Basketball IQ
top.description: Oct 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) looks on from the court after the game against the Dallas Mavericks at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The first month of the 2026-27 NBA season has already been laced with some drama. In this regard, Doc Rivers’ recent comments about his former superstar, Giannis Antetokounmpo , and his basketball IQ garnered considerable attention on social media. During an appearance on “The Bill Simmons Podcast,” former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers claimed that Giannis Antetokounmpo didn’t have a great basketball IQ, often relying on aspects like athleticism and brute force to facilitate his plays. Needless to say, this garnered mixed reactions, though most pushed back on it . In a follow-up interview, Giannis Antetokounmpo admitted that he was caught off guard by his former coach’s comments . While this is largely understandable, according to Andscape’s Marc J. Spears , Doc Rivers has issued an apology to Antetokounmpo while clarifying his message. Spears wrote: “Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers told Andscape on Monday that he reached out to Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo to apologize for a remark he made on a recent podcast.” “Rivers told Andscape that he meant to say ‘feel for the game’ instead of ‘super IQ,’ felt bad about the error, and texted Antetokounmpo an apology, to which the player responded positively.” “I was saying he was one of the most interesting guys,” Rivers added . “He makes unbelievable passes, but then at times, because of his force he plays at, it gets in the way of his feel. It was more of a compliment. I hate this and feel bad about it. I apologize for the distraction. I’m not trying to be one.” Spears also mentioned that Rivers clarified his remarks about saying Giannis Antetokounmpo was among the more difficult players to coach . While this naturally comes across as a slight on the face of it, Rivers stated that it was a “compliment to his greatness.” “The point I was trying to make is whenever you have a great player, you have to fit the team around that great player,” Rivers told Andscape . “That is the point I was trying to make. It’s not always easy. It’s a compliment. I’ve been successful and unsuccessful at it. But your job is to create the best team you can possibly create around that great player and his talents.” For the most part, Rivers’ clarification for criticizing Giannis Antetokounmpo’s basketball IQ makes some sense in the context of the way he plays the game. Since he is often tasked with establishing himself as a threat on the inside, the forward’s decision-making is often compromised, resulting in some unintentional errors. Still, Rivers’ justification for saying the guard is difficult to coach because of his greatness seems somewhat disingenuous. top.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: George Karlaftis #56 and Drue Tranquill #23 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrate after a defensive play against the Los Angeles Chargers in the second quarter of a game at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs have a brutal upcoming stretch on their schedule. It starts on Thanksgiving, as the Chiefs head to Buffalo to take on the Bills. After that is four more games in a row against teams that currently have winning records. However, one of those matchup just got a little bit easier. Kansas City Chiefs Won’t Face WR Puka Nacua During Matchup vs. Rams in Week 13 Rams WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed injured reserve due to MCL and PCL sprains, per HC Sean McVay. pic.twitter.com/ONNnk78zbt — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 According to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Rams are placing star wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve due to MCL and PCL strains in his right knee. He will be required to miss the next four games at minimum, meaning he will not play against the Chiefs on December 3rd on “Thursday Night Football.” That is a huge break for Kansas City’s secondary. The Rams are already down their other top receiver in Davante Adams, who ruptured his hamstring in Week 6. Adams could be back in time to play against the Chiefs, but it will be close. Los Angeles’ offense hasn’t been as explosive as usual this season, and will be even more limited down both Nacua and Adams. Chiefs Have Tough Road to AFC West Division Title Losing to the Denver Broncos in Week 8 was a backbreaker. A win would have assured Kansas City the tiebreaker and given it a two-game lead over Denver. Instead, the two teams are now neck-and-neck, and the Broncos have a much easier remaining schedule than the Chiefs. It will be crucial for Kansas City to not have a letdown against the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons and 3-6 Arizona Cardinals over the next two weeks. Winning those games will get the Chiefs to 8-2 heading into their murderers’ row stretch against the Bills, Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, New England Patriots, and San Francisco 49ers . If the Chiefs are able to reach the postseason, they will certainly be battle-hardened. Hopefully they can find a way to come out of that stretch with more wins than losses. Kansas City will conclude the season with a road matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 17, and a home contest against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 18. top.description: New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV. Getty On Monday, November 9, New York Jets pass rusher Will McDonald requested a trade. A few hours later, head coach Aaron Glenn spoke to the media and gave his reaction to that news. “I just know we’re in the business of keeping good players, so Will’s going to be here,” Glenn responded. Glenn was then asked why McDonald’s playing time has diminished and what happened to him as a player. “I still feel the same about Will, and we try to put him in positions where he’s going to be successful, and we have to continue to do that. That’s one thing between me, (Karl) Dunbar, that we have to continue to do that, also putting him inside. We had a number of packages this week that we felt that were positive for him that he was actually in control of. Will is a good player. He’s a good player and I believe that. We’re going to continue to try to put him in position to go make plays for us,” Glenn said. Glenn was later asked about dealing with a player like McDonald who is frustrated about his role. “Well, I have conversations with him, and me and Will sat down quite a bit the other day and had a really good conversation, and we have a really good relationship. And I think that has a lot to do with it is the communication part of it and whatever that comes out of the communication we try to keep that between us. top.title: UFC chief declines Trump's White House job offer
top.description: White, the 57-year-old president and CEO of UFC, is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year (MANDEL NGAN) Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding." The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. "So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Trump said. "Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody." The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president's announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. - 'Beat the hell out of you' - Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been "having a little fun." "He's a great guy," Trump told the room full of reporters. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you." Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon -- the ring used for UFC fights. "I've always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?" he joked -- before quickliy adding: "I have zero political aspirations." White added that "the last 24 hours of my life has been insane" since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: "I don't tell the president 'no' to anything... I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first." Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sal Stewart has been named the 2026 NL Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year. The Reds first baseman looked like the clear favorite to win over the other two finalists, the Mets’ Carson Benge and the Cardinals’ JJ Wetherholt, for the award. He ended up doing so by a considerable margin, getting 20 of 30 first-place votes and had 170 points overall. Benge was a distant second with 107 points, while Wetherholt finished with 99. BREAKING: Sal Stewart has won the MLB National League Rookie of the Year award 🏆 pic.twitter.com/7EGCktnq7B — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 10, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stewart becomes the ninth player in Cincinnati franchise history to win the award , joining the likes of Pete Rose and Johnny Bench. Jonathan India was the last Reds rookie to win back in 2021. The Reds also became the fifth franchise to have at least nine Rookie of the Year winners, joining the Dodgers, Yankees, Braves, and A’s, per MLB.com. In his first full big league season, Stewart played all 162 games and hit .263 with 32 home runs and 112 RBIs. In doing so, he joined Hall of Famer Frank Robinson as the only Reds to hit 30-plus home runs as a rookie. He also set the franchise rookie record in RBIs and became just the 14th rookie in Major League history with 30 home runs and 100 RBIs . While Stewart’s traditional statistics were spectacular and historic, the advanced statistics told a different story. He had a mere 2.0 WAR per FanGraphs , a distant third behind Wetherholt (4.6) and Benge (4.3). This is in part due to Stewart’s less-than-stellar defense and baserunning compared to the other two. top.title: Cricket Australia chief rules out reopening 'sandpapergate' probe
top.description: Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg (right) and former opening batsman Usman Khawaja chat at a Test match in Brisbane in 2025 (DAVID GRAY) Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg on Tuesday ruled out reopening the investigation into the sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal, saying he did not see "any compelling reason" for a new probe. Opening batsman Usman Khawaja said in his autobiography that the 2018 plot had been common knowledge throughout the team and not limited to a small number of players. The book, released on Tuesday, has reignited the debate over the cheating controversy, in which Australian players were caught using sandpaper to make the ball swing against South Africa. Greenberg said he would consider Khawaja's revelations -- which were on Monday backed as "100 percent accurate" by fellow opener David Warner -- but said there was no need for further action. "We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," he told radio station SEN. "I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that." Captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace after the ball tampering was exposed. A Cricket Australia investigation found they were the only three players with prior knowledge of the plot. But Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, tells a different story in a chapter dedicated to the scandal in his book "Sabr". - 'It was all of us' - "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he told the Sydney Morning Herald at the weekend ahead of the book's release this week. Pat Cummins, now Australia captain, and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in 2021 that they knew about the plot. Darren Lehmann, who was head coach at the time, has also denied there was widespread knowledge among the players. But close friend Warner on Monday released an Instagram video where he said he agreed with Khawaja's version of events. "Uzzie, I throw my full support behind you. I thank you for what you've done," said Warner, who was suspended for 12 months from cricket and received a life ban from any future captaincy or leadership roles for his part in the scandal. "It's 100 percent accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth. It's out there. People wanted to know it. You've come out and said it," he said. "This isn't about reopening old wounds," added Warner, who retired in 2024 after 112 Tests for Australia. "It's about acknowledging that some wounds never properly healed. I stand with my brother Usman Khawaja. "Speaking your truth takes courage, especially when people would rather you stay silent." Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain over his part in the furore during the third Test in Cape Town. Bancroft was slapped with a nine-month ban. sft/dh

nigeria.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future. The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services. It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development. Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need. “That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth. “We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said. Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program. The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities. It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026. The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026. The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities. nigeria.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. nigeria.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028, suspect faces death penalty
nigeria.description: The trial of the man accused of murdering US conservative firebrand Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, the judge said Monday. “Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028,” judge Tony Graf told the Utah district court, noting that 105 days have been reserved for the trial. Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025. The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world. Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities. nigeria.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend. nigeria.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
nigeria.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days. According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions. To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community. They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years. Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families. Full list of eligibility requirements According to IRCC, foreigners seeking permanent residence through the programme must meet the following six requirements: Community recommendation: Obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community in Canada. Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community. Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years. Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test. Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent. Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada. The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada. Applicants are required to satisfy the eligibility conditions and secure the necessary community recommendation and employment offer before applying for permanent residence. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved. “Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.” How the homemade token trick works The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit. Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Each was traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR and then abandoned. None has traded since Nov. 8, and that afternoon the creators of four of them withdrew what liquidity was left. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain. Elliptic first reported the same approach in the laundering of the February 2025 Bybit theft, also attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, when a worthless Tron token helped move at least $24 million. In the Binance case the firm has also seen the technique on Tron and a close variant on Solana that used existing thinly traded tokens rather than homemade ones. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. sports.description: DETROIT — Coach J.B. Bickerstaff was speechless when asked about the Detroit Pistons ' slow starts. He offered no response after the Pistons scored just 14 first-quarter points in Sunday night's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers . Twenty-four hours later, Bickerstaff addressed the Pistons' poor start by changing his starting lineup, which included Daniss Jenkins replacing Paul Reed. The decision left the Pistons with a considerable size disadvantage against one of the league's tallest teams. However, this strategy led to one of their most productive first quarters of the season and a 122-111 victory on Monday night, Nov. 9, inside Little Caesars Arena. Bickerstaff's lineup change addressed the Pistons' struggles that led to their recent two-game losing streak; however, it seemed to benefit John Collins the most. Collins came into the game having scored in double figures once over the previous six games and averaging 6.3 points and 4.7 rebounds. The game against the Lakers was arguably Collins' worst performance, and at times he looked visibly upset with his play. Against the Wizards, Collins set an early tone for the Pistons by scoring nine of the team's first 18 points. Each time the Wizards tried to mount a rally, Collins either scored a timely basket or his defense helped stop Washington's run. While starting at center amid Bickerstaff's lineup change, Collins finished with a season-high 24 points on 9-for-13 shooting and 10 rebounds. The highlight of the night that showcased Collins' motivation to bounce back came at 7:19 in the first quarter, when he completed an alley-oop from Ausar Thompson. The basket forced Wizards coach Brian Keefe to call a timeout. As players walked back to their benches, Collins celebrated passionately. sports.title: Hornets humiliate the Cavs 124-112
sports.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 9: James Harden #1 and Evan Mobley #4 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 9, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers, in desperate need of a get-right game, put together one of their worst performances in recent (regular season) memory by getting blown out by the Charlotte Hornets 124-112 on Monday night. The Cavs fall a game under .500 before heading to New York on Wednesday to play the defending champion Knicks on national television. Instead of using tonight’s game as a momentum builder, the Cavs were laughed out of the arena by the woeful Hornets. Cleveland trailed by as many as 33 points against the NBA’s worst offense in Charlotte, a team that was already missing several key players. Grayson Allen (27 points on 8/14 shooting) and Naz Reid (25 points, 13 rebounds) thoroughly outplayed Cleveland’s starters, resulting in a 16-point deficit at the half. That ballooned to 27 points at the end of the third quarter, leading to none of the Cavs’ starters returning to the game after that. Jarrett Allen returned to the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points and seven rebounds in 19 minutes. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden had 11 points each and combined to shoot 7-20 from the floor. Harden in particular was disastrous, and had some of the worst defensive possessions you will ever see from an NBA player. Evan Mobley had an exceptionally ineffective game, too, with nine points and four turnovers. Harden and Mobley had a combined +/- of -46 tonight, which passes the eye test. Not only did Charlotte’s starters outplay the Cavs, but Cleveland’s backups did too. Craig Porter Jr., Thomas Bryant, Thomas, and Norchad Omier brought the Cavs within eight points late in the fourth quarter before running out of steam. But the reserves showed a lot of heart, and considerably more effort and energy than Cleveland’s starters. The Cavs were out rebounded 49-32 overall, but didn’t get their first offensive rebound until the third quarter, losing that battle 17-3. Cleveland actually ended up with fewer turnovers and shot better from the floor than Charlotte, but the final score didn’t reflect that. This is the type of loss that reverberates through an organization, especially one that is expensive and on a fixed timeline like the Cavs. There is a heightened sense of urgency to right the ship, but Cleveland remains exceptionally inconsistent and underwhelming. Despite quality wins against Minnesota and Philadelphia, the Cavs feel like a team teetering on the edge of the abyss. Losses like tonight’s are what push things over.

Glenn was then asked why McDonald’s playing time has diminished and what happened to him as a player. “I still feel the same about Will, and we try to put him in positions where he’s going to be successful, and we have to continue to do that. That’s one thing between me, (Karl) Dunbar, that we have to continue to do that, also putting him inside. We had a number of packages this week that we felt that were positive for him that he was actually in control of. Will is a good player. He’s a good player and I believe that. We’re going to continue to try to put him in position to go make plays for us,” Glenn said. Glenn was later asked about dealing with a player like McDonald who is frustrated about his role. “Well, I have conversations with him, and me and Will sat down quite a bit the other day and had a really good conversation, and we have a really good relationship. sports.title: UFC chief declines Trump's White House job offer
sports.description: White, the 57-year-old president and CEO of UFC, is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year (MANDEL NGAN) Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding." The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. "So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Trump said. "Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody." The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president's announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. - 'Beat the hell out of you' - Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been "having a little fun." "He's a great guy," Trump told the room full of reporters. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you." Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon -- the ring used for UFC fights. "I've always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?" he joked -- before quickliy adding: "I have zero political aspirations." White added that "the last 24 hours of my life has been insane" since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: "I don't tell the president 'no' to anything... I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first." Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. dk/msp

sports.title: Cricket Australia chief rules out reopening 'sandpapergate' probe
sports.description: Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg (right) and former opening batsman Usman Khawaja chat at a Test match in Brisbane in 2025 (DAVID GRAY) Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg on Tuesday ruled out reopening the investigation into the sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal, saying he did not see "any compelling reason" for a new probe. Opening batsman Usman Khawaja said in his autobiography that the 2018 plot had been common knowledge throughout the team and not limited to a small number of players. The book, released on Tuesday, has reignited the debate over the cheating controversy, in which Australian players were caught using sandpaper to make the ball swing against South Africa. Greenberg said he would consider Khawaja's revelations -- which were on Monday backed as "100 percent accurate" by fellow opener David Warner -- but said there was no need for further action. "We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again," he told radio station SEN. "I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that." Captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace after the ball tampering was exposed. A Cricket Australia investigation found they were the only three players with prior knowledge of the plot. But Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, tells a different story in a chapter dedicated to the scandal in his book "Sabr". - 'It was all of us' - "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he told the Sydney Morning Herald at the weekend ahead of the book's release this week. Pat Cummins, now Australia captain, and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in 2021 that they knew about the plot. Darren Lehmann, who was head coach at the time, has also denied there was widespread knowledge among the players. But close friend Warner on Monday released an Instagram video where he said he agreed with Khawaja's version of events. "Uzzie, I throw my full support behind you. I thank you for what you've done," said Warner, who was suspended for 12 months from cricket and received a life ban from any future captaincy or leadership roles for his part in the scandal. "It's 100 percent accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth. It's out there. People wanted to know it. You've come out and said it," he said. "This isn't about reopening old wounds," added Warner, who retired in 2024 after 112 Tests for Australia. "It's about acknowledging that some wounds never properly healed. I stand with my brother Usman Khawaja. "Speaking your truth takes courage, especially when people would rather you stay silent." Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain over his part in the furore during the third Test in Cape Town. Bancroft was slapped with a nine-month ban. sft/dh

sports.title: The Rams need Matthew Stafford to play like an MVP

Stafford currently has 16 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 90.6 passer rating. That is functional. It’s nowhere near “MVP” level. Last year Stafford was manufacturing big-time throws and taking care of the football. He has always been prone to mistakes. But this year has reached a higher frequency and there is less of the good to offset. The gap is evident in the efficiency metrics that separate good from elite. Stafford’s big-time throw rate has cratered from 7.7% to roughly 3% this year. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) offensive grade sits in the upper 60’s, good for no better than 20th among qualified quarterbacks. That is not the profile of a player who is elevating the offense around him. It’s the mark of someone who is mostly managing a system, if not part of the problem. The distinction matters because the supporting cast has not been built to absorb a decline in quarterback play. The Rams spent all offseason retooling their defense. The tradeoff brought minimal reinforcements on offense. Puka Nacua, who will now miss at least the next four games , has been asked to handle an outsized share of targets and production. Even when Nacua is available, the rest of the skill players have failed to consistently generate explosive plays. The run game has taken a step forward in stretches. technology.title: Attackers backdoor trusted AWS integrations to steal secrets
technology.description: Unknown attackers used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments, stealing secrets and other sensitive data from S3 buckets. Qubole is a cloud data processing platform that uses cross-account IAM roles to manage compute and access storage in customers' AWS environments without requiring customers to provide long-lived AWS access keys. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions. Neither AWS nor Qubole responded to The Register 's inquiries. Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders after AI data security company Sentra flagged suspicious activity, traced the malicious activity back to October 14, when credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account were used to call the sts:AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for customer-managed integration roles. The calls originated from Qubole AWS account 805246085872 , and used IAM user ID AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS , Wiz analysts Zack Morrow, Sean Johnstone, and Benjamin Read said in a Monday blog about the supply chain attack. “Across the affected environments, Wiz CIRT has not observed this IAM user in any activity other than that associated with this threat actor,” the trio wrote. This activity continued on October 15, and on October 18, the digital intruders began using a second IAM user from the same account. Once inside customers’ environments, the crooks began probing a ton of AWS services and stealing credentials, keys, and other secrets stored across Lambda, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store. The miscreants also used TruffleHog to test AWS credentials belonging to victim organizations, discover their Microsoft Entra ID secrets, and request OAuth tokens using Okta client credentials also uncovered while snooping around the AWS environments. Abusing the integration roles also allowed the criminals to steal data from customers’ S3 storage, although it seems they were largely opportunistic attackers, in some cases downloading entire buckets, as opposed to state-sponsored spies looking for specific data. The threat hunters haven’t attributed the supply chain attack to any particular group, and say they don’t have any insight into how the miscreants are using the stolen data. science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Roger C. Wiens, SuperCam Principal Investigator for NASA’s Perseverance rover at Purdue University Nov. 4, 2026 Exploration on Mars turns up the unexpected. Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. However, large meteor and asteroid impacts can create local metamorphism due to long-term heating from the impact. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. science.title: NYT bestseller ‘Robopocalypse’ is getting a TV series with Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman at the helm

Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement. science.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts
science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space.
